messages:
Priya (Support): @channel heads up — getting a spike of customer reports about 5xx errors from the hosted /v1/generate endpoint starting ~2024-05-09 14:03 UTC. Customers see 502/503 and timeouts. Examples in CS-3245 and CS-3246.

Cathy (Customer): FYI — our app started returning 503s at 14:05. Error message from client: "upstream returned 502 Bad Gateway". We have x-request-id: 01FZ8A2H9Q9X and session-id: sess_9f2a. This is blocking our critical flows.

Priya (Support): Logged initial ticket INC-2026 and notified SRE. Adding logs from the customer: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
x-request-id: 01FZ8A2H9Q9X
x-customer: acme-inc
Response: 502 Bad Gateway
Body: {"error":"control_plane_unavailable","detail":"routing policy service returned 500"}
```

Alex (SRE): I'm on it. Looking at control-plane metrics and traces now. First glance: elevated error rate from the routing-policy service and increased p99 latency on auth/session store reads.

sre-bot: alert: routing-policy-service error rate > 5% (14:02–14:20 UTC), config-db read timeouts spike, circuit-breaker triggered for downstream model-router.

Alex (SRE): Correlated trace for x-request-id 01FZ8A2H9Q9X shows: auth-service session lookup -> routing-policy -> config-db read -> timeout -> routing-policy returns 500 -> gateway returns 502 to client.

Javier (Eng-Platform): We had a config-db schema migration rolled out 13:55 UTC to add an index (rollback-able), small change but could increase connection churn. Any chance the migration caused long-held locks or increased query plans?

Alex (SRE): Possible. Current logs from routing-policy show repeated failures: 
```
ERROR routing-policy: failed to resolve route for model gpt-small: config-db read timeout after 1.5s; attempts=3
ERROR auth: session lookup error: deadline exceeded; user=session:sess_9f2a
WARN gateway: upstream routing-policy returned 500; returning 502 to client
```

Priya (Support): Customers reporting degraded experience + increased errors and some timeouts on retries. Billing team flagged potential revenue impact for dedicated tenants.

Maya (Billing): Tracking ACME and several dedicated customers. If this persists >30m, we need to pre-authorize credits per SLO policy. Keep me updated with ETA.

Alex (SRE): Quick repro steps for engineers: 
1) curl reproducer with a known session header and x-request-id: 
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "x-request-id: repro-$(date +%s)" \
  -H "x-session-id: sess_9f2a" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"hello"}'
```
2) tail routing-policy logs filtering by x-request-id and config-db errors.

Alex (SRE): Immediate mitigation options I propose: 
- Increase config-db read timeout and connection pool temporarily to absorb traffic.
- Bypass routing-policy for cached/default routing (fallback to default route) for hosted API traffic for 10m windows.
- Roll back the recent schema migration if we confirm it's correlated.

Javier (Eng-Platform): I'm rolling a hotfix that skips the new index usage and increases DB connection pool from 50->150 on the config-db read replicas. Will deploy to canary region first.

Priya (Support): Noted. I'll update CS tickets and ask impacted customers for x-request-ids and sample payloads. 

Alex (SRE): Deployed a temporary route fallback at 14:27 UTC for public tenants — this should reduce 502s while we stabilize routing-policy. Monitoring p50/p99 now.

sre-bot: info: fallback-route enabled by Alex (SRE) at 14:27 UTC. error-rate for /v1/generate dropped from 6.4% -> 1.2% over 5m.

Cathy (Customer): Thanks — errors reduced on our side around 14:30. Still seeing occasional timeouts but much better.

Alex (SRE): Followup actions (assigned): 
- [Alex] Roll back problematic migration if traces show lock contention (in progress).
- [Javier] DB pool increase and index toggle (in progress).
- [Priya] Customer comms: update CS-3245/3246, include mitigation steps and ETA.
- [SRE] Create post-incident task to add fine-grained tracing for control-plane RPCs and default fallback for routing-policy.

Maya (Billing): I'll hold off on credits until the incident is fully resolved; please add time windows and affected tenants to INC-2026.

Javier (Eng-Platform): Canary looks good. Rolling to primaries now. Also added a temporary config flag: routing.policy.timeout_ms=2000 -> 4000 for 1h.

Alex (SRE): After DB pool bump and fallback, error rate stabilized. Closing the high-severity window but keeping incident open for RCA.

incidents-bot: incident INC-2026 severity downgraded to SEV-2 at 15:12 UTC — customer-impact mitigated; RCA owner needed.

Priya (Support): Thanks all. RCA notes to include: control-plane dependency (config-db) experienced read timeouts after a schema migration increased query cost/connection churn; routing-policy had no graceful fallback until we enabled default route; auth/session timeouts propagated and surface as 502/503 to clients.

Alex (SRE): Proposed long-term fixes: 
- Add circuit-breaker + cached default-route for routing-policy to avoid full-request blocking.
- Database query optimization and safer migration rollout (throttle schema changes, pre-warm connections).
- Increase observability: per-RPC latency buckets, more logging on session store misses.

Priya (Support): ACTION ITEMS: open RCA doc, assign owner (Alex), draft customer update for affected tenants, coordinate with billing for any required credits.

Cathy (Customer): Appreciate the fast response. Please share ETA for permanent fix and postmortem when available.

Priya (Support): Will follow up in CS-3245 with postmortem link once ready. Closing thread for now — will append RCA and timeline. :white_check_mark:
